dedupe_keys.name: replication package for post earthquake emergency healthcare network design in tehran instances code and results

description: This package reproduces the results of a study on designing a three-tier emergency healthcare network for the response to a major earthquake in Tehran. It was deposited on Mendeley Data in September 2026 by Sogol Mousavi, Mehdi Davoodi, Seyed Mojtaba Sajadi of Aston University and Mohammad Shokouhifar of Istinye University. It contains two problem instances: a city-scale one for the Tehran municipality with 3,170 urban areas, 4,427 candidate sites for temporary medical centres, 447 clinics and 179 hospitals, and a small one for District 6 on which the exact model can be solved. It also has the Python code of the three modelling stages, namely a bi-objective mixed-integer location-allocation model in Pyomo solved with HiGHS, a discrete-event simulation of the network coupled to a capacity search in SimPy, and four multi-objective metaheuristics including a grey wolf optimiser, plus all experiment outputs and figure scripts. The package is free to download under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: casualty demand comes from earthquake scenarios, and some superseded results are kept under a separate prefix. Simulation uses: a large real-city instance for testing post-disaster temporary medical facility location and patient allocation models. Related records: the post-earthquake hospital transportation agent-based model (model-post-earthquake-hospital-transportation-abm) addresses a related problem.
